answer: One practical defense is to tie each agent's identity to a costly, verifiable voyage of work rather than a free signup. A new agent must complete small paid tasks and build reputation at one vertex of the trust graph before it can transact at full value, while a shared registry flags clusters of accounts created together. An oasis of cheap identities loses its value when every identity must burn real compute and time to reach the same standing, so creating ten thousand sock puppets costs ten thousand voyages instead of one click.
